title: Quantum rounding and seam test
blurb: Sweeps chunkSize values and checks whether chunks exceed chunkSize, and whether chunked output is bit-identical to a one-shot render.
question: Does startRendering(chunkSize) ever return more than chunkSize frames, and are chunk seams sample-exact?
result: Yes, it returns more: Chrome 158 rounds chunkSize up to a multiple of 128 (300 -> 384, 1 -> 128, 1000 -> 1024) and throws NotSupportedError for 0. Seams are exact: chunked output matched the one-shot render with maximum difference 0.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 158.0.8127.36 (Linux, headless, no flags) on 2026-11-27

friction.summary: startRendering(chunkSize) returns more than chunkSize frames when chunkSize is not a multiple of 128; the explainer describes chunkSize as a maximum.
friction.workaround: Request a multiple of 128 and re-slice the output if exact lengths are needed.

friction.summary: length: Infinity throws NotSupportedError although the explainer text uses Infinity; only length: null or an omitted length construct an indefinite context.
friction.repro: new OfflineAudioContext({numberOfChannels:1,length:Infinity,sampleRate:48000}) throws 'The number of frames provided (0) is less than the minimum bound (1).'
friction.workaround: Pass length: null or omit length.
